'''Ahokini''', officially the '''Republic of Ahokini'''. It is bordered by [[Quidic]] to the east and [[Verste]] to the south. The country has a population of [[List of countries and dependencies by population|approximately twenty million]]. Its capital and most populous city is [[Ribash]]. The country is renowned for its ancient temples, including the [[Global Heritage Site]] of [[Krulasas Ligen]], and for showcasing a diverse range of [[Architectural styles in Ahokini|architectural styles]] from various historical eras.

The country traces its cultural identity to in the [[Esnanan Dynasty]], which invaded and settled the western coast of [[Ankuano]] in the 11th century, creating the [[Kingdom of Shuoshu]]. Through its location, the kingdom was a hub for maritime trade. In the 1560s, [[Ast Kauria]] collapsed and many kingdoms were established, importantly, the [[Kingdom of Furaku]] was established. In 1893, the kingdom was unified under [[Ashain|Ashaini]] protection and integrated into the main Empire. Ahokini was under [[Ashaini administration of Ahokini|Ashaini administration]] during the [[Red War]], gaining partial independence in 1695. The country regained full independence in 1705 as the Republic of Ahokini. A [[Ahokini Civil War|Civil War]] from 1703 to 1711 saw the r[[Erirroea|ight-leaning dictatorship faction]], supported by [[Estijan]], oppose the [[wikipedia:Communism|communists]]], backed by the [[Dahe|Dahens]]. The war ended with the establishment of the Republic in 1711, a communist state, until its dissolution in 1739.

Ahokini performs well in metrics of education, [[List of countries by Krali Total Development Index|human development]], and innovation. Its citizens enjoy one of the [[List of countries by life expectancy|world's longest life expectancies]] and access to some of the [[wikipedia:Internet_access|fastest Internet connection]] speeds and densest [[wikipedia:High-speed_rail|high-speed railway]] networks. Since the turn of the late 17th century, the country has been renowned for its globally influential [[Ahokini music culture|music culture,]] particularly in music.
